summary: AMASS auth improvements fully verified end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest cases pass covering enumeration-safe /api/auth/forgot-password (identical 200 bodies for known+unknown emails), /api/auth/reset-password 400 for wrong code, full happy-path (register throwaway -> forgot -> Mongo code_hash injection -> reset -> login with new password), brute-force lockout (6 wrong attempts -> 7th 429 with 'Try again in N minute(s)' + correct password also rejected while locked). Frontend: intro sequence (AMASS -> FIXA crossfade, Skip always visible, amass_brand_intro_seen_v1 persists, Fixa does not replay on second launch), /login (forgot-password-link navigates, show-password toggle flips input type password->text, wrong creds show 'Invalid email or password' testID=login-error, demo creds succeed -> tabs, redirect preserve /login?redirect=/wallet -> /wallet), /forgot-password (step1 -> step2 with 'Resend code in Ns' countdown, wrong code shows fp-error 'That code is invalid or has expired. Request a new one.', back-to-sign-in works), /register (invalid email + short password inline validation on reg-error, existing email -> 'This email is already registered. Try signing in instead.', new unique email -> tabs home, Google button present). Throwaway users and lockout rows cleaned from Mongo after run. No blocking issues found.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: 'Animated: useNativeDriver is not supported because the native animated module is missing. Falling back to JS-based animation.' This is expected on web preview (RCTAnimation unavailable) and will go away on native builds; no action needed unless you want to silence by setting useNativeDriver:false on web via Platform.OS.

Console warning: 'shadow* style props are deprecated. Use boxShadow.' Appears globally across screens. Reference: likely in /app/frontend/src/constants/theme.ts or component style sheets using shadowColor/shadowOffset/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius. Migrate to the boxShadow shorthand.

Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents.' Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:81 (`<Animated.View pointerEvents=...>`) and /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:89 (`<SafeAreaView ... pointerEvents="box-none">`). Move pointerEvents into style.

action_items: (cosmetic) Migrate shadow* style props to boxShadow and move pointerEvents into style={} to clear repeated web console warnings.
(cosmetic) Consider setting useNativeDriver:false when Platform.OS === 'web' in app/index.tsx Animated.timing/spring to silence the web warning.
critical_code_review_comments: auth_security.py enumeration-safety is correct: identical {ok,message} body regardless of account presence, and send_email failures are swallowed to the same payload so provider state doesn't leak.
Reset code is stored as sha256 hash with 15-min TTL + 5 verify attempts + 1 send/min + 5 sends/hour: matches playbook.
Lockout logic resets fails to 0 after locking and relies on locked_until window - sensible; correct password is also rejected while locked (verified).
forgot-password.tsx useEffect dep array uses `cooldown > 0` (boolean) which triggers the eslint-disable-line already in place; works correctly in testing (countdown ticks every second).
seed_data_creation: Created and deleted two throwaway users during testing: test_amass_<uuid>@amasstest.io (reset flow) and test_amass_<uuid>@amasstest.io (lockout flow). Also created test<uuid>@amasstest.io via UI register flow; all three were deleted from users/password_resets/login_attempts collections after run. Confirmed demo@amass.africa login_attempts cleared so demo is not locked.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_auth_forgot_reset_lockout.py is self-contained (creates/cleans its own throwaway users, uses lowercase emails because server lowercases on write). Run with: python -m pytest backend/tests/test_auth_forgot_reset_lockout.py -v -o 'addopts='. The project's pytest.ini configures xdist with loadscope which is compatible. Mongo is accessed via pymongo (sync) to avoid motor cross-event-loop issues inside pytest fixtures. Email provider (Emergent Resend) actually sends during /forgot-password; the test never relies on retrieving the real code - it injects a known sha256(code) directly into password_resets.
